title: API groups
description: Validates metadata/api/api-groups/*.yaml — the gateway's route policy. The gateway builds its entire route table from this file and holds none in code. Cross-checked at boot against metadata/api/service-registry.v1.yaml: every prefix must be claimed by the service it names, and a service declaring api_groups: [] must not appear here at all.

defaults.description: Applied to any group that omits the field. Defaults are deliberately the restrictive values so that forgetting a field cannot open a route.

authentication.description: none is permitted only where a session cannot exist yet — registration, login, OTP, recovery.

audit.description: Gateway-level audit. none leaves auditing to the owning service at the point of vault access; writes covers POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; all covers reads too, for groups where the read is itself the sensitive act.

role.description: Matches the actor_role CHECK constraint on core.sessions.

prefix.description: Must appear in the owning service's api_groups list in the service registry.

roles.description: Empty only when authentication is none. A group reachable with a session but permitting no role is unreachable, and the gateway rejects that at boot rather than serving 403 forever.

purpose.description: Must be a registered id in metadata/consent/purpose-registry/. Required whenever audit is not none, because audit_events.purpose is NOT NULL and references a registered purpose.

step_up.description: Requires a live step-up assertion on the session, scoped to this group. Step-up assertions expire sooner than the session (backend-requirements §5).

step_up_grant.description: Responses from this group may stamp a step-up assertion onto the caller's session. Only where a second factor is actually verified. The gateway owns the session record, so a service cannot amend one itself; this names the one group whose verified answer it will act on, and the scope it grants is checked against the groups that require step-up.

session_cookie.description: The gateway issues the HttpOnly session cookie from this group's responses, and clears it when one revokes a session. Only where a session is minted. A downstream service cannot set a cookie on our origin — the proxy strips set-cookie — so this is the only way the browser is given a credential, and naming the group here keeps that to one place rather than a body sniff on every route.

then.description: An audited group must name the purpose it will record. audit_events.purpose is NOT NULL.
An unauthenticated group has no actor to authorise, to step up, or to attribute an audit event to.
An authenticated group must permit at least one role.
